chi_convention.production_formula: cavity.chi_dispersive_koch(g, f01, f_r, alpha), Delta = f01 - f_r
chi_convention.truth_standard: cavity.chi_two_pole(g, f01, f12, f_r, r), r = (n12/n01)^2 exact
chi_convention.superseded_formula: cavity.chi_dispersive(g, f_r - f01, alpha) -- retained, never called in production

harmonic_limit_identity.statement: chi_two_pole(r = 2) == chi_dispersive_koch identically; that identity is what fixes Delta = f01 - f_r as the single formula's convention

pole_locations_GHz.statement: the corrected forms are singular only at the 0-1 and 1-2 lines; the reference convention moves the second pole to f01 + |alpha| = 42.2290 GHz, where the transmon has no transition

chi_convention.impact: the superseded recommended point (f_r = 44.5966 GHz, chi/kappa = 1.0092) fails: its corrected chi/kappa is 0.424 (Koch) / 0.466 (two-pole). The whole f_r > f01 window is empty analytically. The design moves below f01 into the gap-protection window.

gap_protection_window.derivation: f01 lies inside the Maxwell-scaled readout lattice's TE gap iff gap_lo f_r/f_cav <= f01 <= gap_hi f_r/f_cav, i.e. f01 f_cav/gap_hi <= f_r <= f01 f_cav/gap_lo
gap_protection_window.meaning: inside this window the readout mirror region is a photonic bandgap AT the qubit frequency, which is what the missing-T1-channel radiation finding asks for. The superseded recommended point at 44.5966 GHz lies outside it; the corrected one lies inside.

reference_convention_scan.flag: REFERENCE CONVENTION, RETAINED, NOT A DESIGN WINDOW -- every chi below was produced with the inverted detuning Delta = f_r - f01 (cavity.chi_dispersive). Reproduced bit-for-bit from the superseded artifact so nothing is deleted; superseded for every design purpose by the corrected blocks. Mirrors the AT-6 small-frequency precedent (paper/decisions.md 2026-07-27 M6 P3).

recommended_point.kappa_ceiling_MHz_flag: SUPERSEDED FORMULA (CEIL) with Delta_r = f_r - f01; retained so this block reproduces the pre-correction artifact. The corrected (CEIL') value at the same detuning is in corrected_values_at_this_point.

corrected_values_at_this_point.verdict: FAILS chi/kappa >= 1 under both corrected constructions; the point is withdrawn

above_f01_emptiness_proof.verdict: EMPTY -- no f_r > f01 satisfies chi/kappa >= 1, T1_Purcell >= 30 us and kappa >= f_r/Q_i simultaneously

analytic.sup_formula: sqrt(|alpha| / (2 pi T1_min)), the D -> inf limit of (CEIL')
analytic.statement: the Koch ceiling never reaches the measured internal-Q linewidth anywhere in the mandated window; no grid is needed

sweep.two_pole_note: the exact-element ceiling grows like sqrt(D) and DOES cross kappa_int, but only far outside the mandated window and far outside the gap-protection window; inside the mandated window it stays below

envelope.note: kappa_max is the closed-form largest linewidth admitting ANY g at that f_r, after chi/kappa >= 1 (Koch AND two-pole), the Purcell margin 1.2x, (g/Delta)^2 <= 0.01 and (g12/Delta12)^2 <= 0.01. eta_ceiling = 1 - kappa_int/kappa_max is therefore the exact upper bound on the readout port efficiency at that frequency.

koch_only_optimum.flag: TWO_POLE_SCREEN DISABLED -- reaches a higher eta but its exact two-pole chi/kappa is below 1, so it is NOT recommended. Exported for completeness and so the cost of the C8 screen is explicit.

grid.brief_grid_note: the naive AT-5 scan used d_eff in {100, 200} um only; d_eff = 50 um is a P5 addition

counts.verdict: under the REFERENCE convention the naive 22-point window became 12 on the same grid (14 with the 50 um column) and 0 once the measured kappa floor was enforced. Under the CORRECTED chi the same mandated grid gives 11 / 11 / 0: the f_r > f01 window is empty at every stage, and `above_f01_emptiness_proof` shows it is empty for every detuning and every d_eff, not merely on this grid.

recommended_point.corridor_note: the recommended point maximises eta, so by construction it sits where C7 (upper) and C8 (lower) both nearly bind and its d_eff window is only 0.35 um wide (0.58% of the electrode). corridor_vs_kappa shows the trade: backing kappa off widens the window roughly linearly in the eta given up. This is a fabrication-tolerance statement, not a feasibility one.
recommended_point.objective: maximise the readout port efficiency eta = 1 - kappa_int/kappa subject to |chi_Koch|/kappa >= 1, |chi_two_pole|/kappa >= 1 (C8), (g/Delta)^2 <= 0.01 with Delta = f01 - f_r, (g12/Delta_12)^2 <= 0.01 (C7), kappa_r >= kappa_int(f_r) and a Purcell margin T1/30us >= 1.2; unchanged from the superseded run except for the corrected chi and the two added constraints

margin_efficiency_front.note: eta falls linearly in the margin and hits zero at m = R = 1.6525. Trading the recommended point's Purcell margin for readout efficiency (or the reverse) moves along this line; nothing outside it is reachable without lifting C2 (higher Q_i) or C3 (a Purcell filter). Rows with kappa above 3.7868 MHz are additionally excluded by the dispersivity caps C7/(g/Delta)^2 and are flagged infeasible.

deviation_vs_exploration_precomputation.verdict: the exploration point is reproduced to 1e-15 on every quantity it reports, and is then REJECTED by the new constraint C7: its (g12/Delta_12)^2 = 0.01858 is 1.86x the cap. The rejection is not marginal -- with C7 enforced the largest kappa admitting any g at f_r = 39.2589 GHz is 1.8110 MHz, below kappa_int = 2.6868 MHz, so that f_r supports no operating point at all. This export therefore SUPERSEDES both the exploration's eta ~ 0.20 trade point and the ruling's description of it as 'marginal'.

maxwell_scaling.relation: a_r = a * f_cav / f_r   (nu = a/lambda invariant at fixed r/a, t/a, eps_core)
maxwell_scaling.V_mode_scaling_check: cavity.readout_window_scan already uses V_r = V_mode (f_cav/f_r)^3, which is identically V_mode_a3 * a_r^3 -- the scan and this geometry are the same scaling, no new assumption.

f_r_in_readout_lattice.note: true by construction: Maxwell scaling maps the measured 145 GHz / [137.5, 177.9] GHz placement onto a_r rigidly, so the readout line keeps the same +7.5 / -32.9 GHz margins scaled by f_r/f_cav. photonics.json:tolerances (|dr/a|<=2%, |dt/a|<=5%, |da|<=2%) also scales rigidly.

f_r_in_drive_lattice.verdict: FAR BELOW the drive lattice's TE gap: at a/lambda = 0.0733 the hole lattice is deeply subwavelength (lambda/a = 13.6), so the drive lattice is not a mirror at f_r -- it homogenises into an index-guiding slab of volume-average eps ~ 8.19 (air fill fraction 0.3265). The readout mode PROPAGATES there and is guided away laterally.
f_r_in_drive_lattice.homogenisation_caveat: volume average only; Maxwell-Garnett / full-wave effective index would differ by a few percent. No new FDTD run.

f_cav_in_readout_lattice.verdict: at a_r/lambda = 1.0991, i.e. 3.873x the fundamental cavity-line nu, the 145 GHz drive tone is far above the readout lattice's first TE gap and lies in its higher-order band manifold.
f_cav_in_readout_lattice.PARAMETRIC_CAVEAT: whether 145 GHz lands inside a higher-order gap of the readout lattice is NOT computed here -- it needs an MPB/FDTD band run at a_r, which is out of P5 scope. The default design assumption is the pessimistic one: higher-order bands are dense, so the readout lattice does NOT confine 145 GHz. This is a parametric caveat, not a computed result.

gap_positions.symmetry_verdict: NEITHER lattice confines the other's frequency. Each cavity needs its own mirror region, and each region is transparent (or leaky) at the other's frequency.

length_scales_um.mode_extent_convention: V_mode_a3^(1/3) * a (cube-root of the measured modal volume)
length_scales_um.chip_rule: >=15x15 periods (~9x9 mm) to suppress in-plane leakage

concepts.name: side-by-side (butted lattice regions)
concepts.description: Two rectangular photonic-crystal regions sharing a straight interface; each L3 defect buried behind its own 8 outer mirror rows; the qubit island sits at the interface and reaches each cavity centre through a routed trace.
concepts.reason: the minimum centre-to-centre distance is 19.81 mm, so at least one collection electrode becomes a >1 mm routed trace. P2's divider assumes an electrically small lumped pickup (C_c = kappa_geo eps0 eps_eff d_eff); a mm-scale trace adds capacitance that is not in the C_Sigma budget and is a distributed element at 40-60 GHz. The lumped beta model, and with it the whole P2/P5 coupling chain, breaks.

concepts.name: shared interface defect (heterostructure seam)
concepts.description: A single defect straddling the seam, with drive-lattice mirrors on one side and readout-lattice mirrors on the other.
concepts.reason: confinement is one-sided at BOTH frequencies: the readout-lattice side is transparent at 145 GHz (higher-order bands) and the drive-lattice side is a homogenised eps ~ 8.19 slab at 37.44 GHz. A mode bounded on only one side is not a resonator; both Q's collapse to the open-slab radiation value.

concepts.name: nested / concentric heterostructure (RECOMMENDED)
concepts.description: The complete drive-lattice patch (its L3 defect plus its mirror rows) is embedded at the CENTRE of the readout lattice's L3 defect region. Both field maxima then coincide at one point, where the island and both short collection electrodes sit. At f_r the drive patch is a homogenised eps ~ 8.19 dielectric plug inside the readout defect -- a perturbation of the readout mode, not a mirror.
concepts.reason: with the measured 8 outer mirror rows the drive patch spans 9.89 mm against a 6.82 mm readout L3 defect, so it overruns by 0.78 readout mirror rows per side. Either the drive cavity is cut back to ~5.0 mirror rows (Q_i then unverified -- the measured 14611 assumes 8 rows in a 24a cell), or the readout defect is enlarged beyond L3. Both need an FDTD run at a_r; DESIGN ESTIMATE, not a computed Q.
concepts.island_placement: island at the common centre; d_eff_drive = 20 um and d_eff_readout = O(60 um) are 0.0341 and 0.0264 of the respective lattice constants, so both pickups stay electrically small and the P2 lumped divider survives.

f_r_in_readout_lattice.note: true by construction: Maxwell scaling maps the measured 145 GHz / [137.5, 177.9] GHz placement onto a_r rigidly, so the readout line keeps the same +7.5 / -32.9 GHz margins scaled by f_r/f_cav. photonics.json:tolerances (|dr/a|<=2%, |dt/a|<=5%, |da|<=2%) also scales rigidly.

The readout mode PROPAGATES there and is guided away laterally.
f_r_in_drive_lattice.homogenisation_caveat: volume average only; Maxwell-Garnett / full-wave effective index would differ by a few percent. No new FDTD run.

The default design assumption is the pessimistic one: higher-order bands are dense, so the readout lattice does NOT confine 145 GHz. This is a parametric caveat, not a computed result.

brief_grid.impossible: kappa_target 1 MHz <= kappa_intrinsic 3.257 MHz: no value of N reaches it, the cavity is already broader than the target.
kappa_target 3 MHz <= kappa_intrinsic 3.257 MHz: no value of N reaches it, the cavity is already broader than the target.

purcell_filter_N.caveat: the ladder fit ln Q_w = sigma N + b is measured from TWO points (N = 3, 4; photonics.json flags trivial_r2_warning), and it is applied at a_r by Maxwell scale invariance of Q_w (a purely geometric/radiative quantity). No FDTD ladder has been run at a_r.

purcell_filter_element.caveat: standard single-pole bandpass-filter estimate; no FDTD of a photonic-crystal filter at a_r has been run. It is the escape hatch from the (CEIL) kappa ceiling: with the Purcell constraint lifted, kappa_r is limited only by chi/kappa >= 1, and the readout port efficiency eta can be pushed toward 1.

formulas.n_drive: n = (P_in/(hbar*omega_d)) * kappa_ext / (Delta_qr^2 + (kappa/2)^2); kappa, kappa_ext, Delta_qr in rad/s, P_in in W, omega_d = 2 pi f_drive
formulas.rabi: Omega_R = 2 g sqrt(n_drive); quoted as Omega_R/2pi in Hz
formulas.leakage: Lorentzian photon response of a mode at detuning, (kappa/2)^2 / (Delta^2 + (kappa/2)^2)

leakage.caveat: Lorentzian mode filtering only. The port-to-far-cavity coupling coefficient (how much of a tone injected at the readout port even reaches the drive cavity's near field) is a layout quantity and is NOT modelled -- these dB figures are the on-chip frequency selectivity, not the total isolation.

pair_breaking.statement: LINEAR (single-photon) audit only, carried over from P3 unchanged: h f_r < 2 Delta(nu) over |nu + 2.4| < 0.4111, i.e. essentially the whole superconducting dome, with a 3.089x margin at the apex. The readout tone is therefore not pair-breaking at any power in this model.
pair_breaking.PARAMETRIC_CAVEAT: photon-ASSISTED (multi-photon) pair breaking is NOT modelled. The naive order is n_gamma >= 2 Delta / (h f_r) = 3.089, i.e. a 4-photon process at the readout frequency; its rate depends on an unmodelled nonlinearity and on the intracavity photon number. Nothing here bounds it -- it is flagged, not computed.

constraints.name: shared C_Sigma budget (P2)
constraints.meaning: at kappa_geo = 2.0 and eps_eff = 6.34, any d_eff_readout above 86.9 um oversubscribes the island and forces the common-process rescale. The brief's 100 um sample point sits above the knee (oversubscription 1.1227); the recommended 60.0 um sits BELOW it, so the oversubscription finding is resolved, not merely rescaled.

constraints.name: measured internal-Q linewidth floor (P5, new)
constraints.statement: kappa_r >= f_r / Q_i, Q_i scale-invariant from photonics.json
constraints.meaning: the brief's kappa_r grid {1, 3} MHz lies at or below this floor (2.562 MHz at f_r = 37.439 GHz), so every kappa = 1 MHz row of the naive feasible set is physically unreachable with the measured cavity.

constraints.name: analytic Purcell/dispersive kappa ceiling (P5; CORRECTED 2026-07-27)
constraints.statement: kappa_r^2 <= |alpha| |Delta| / (|Delta + alpha| 2 pi T1_min), Delta = f01 - f_r
constraints.superseded_statement: kappa_r^2 <= |alpha| Delta_r / ((Delta_r + alpha) 2 pi T1_min) with Delta_r = f_r - f01 -- the inverted-detuning form; it gave 3.8249 MHz at Delta_r = 4 GHz against the corrected 2.4799 MHz, and it decreased in Delta_r where the corrected ceiling increases
constraints.meaning: chi/kappa >= 1 and T1_Purcell >= 30 us cannot both hold above this kappa, for ANY g and hence any d_eff. Under the corrected chi it INCREASES with detuning above f01 and saturates at 2.9428 MHz, which is below kappa_int everywhere in the mandated 4-16 GHz window -- so that window is EMPTY (see above_f01_emptiness_proof). Below f01 the ceiling is much wider because |Delta + alpha| = |f_r - f12| can be small, and that is where the design now sits.

constraints.name: readout port efficiency squeeze (C2 + C3 + C7)

superseded_value.flag: REFERENCE CONVENTION -- the 'eta <= 20.2 % anywhere, 11.5 % at the recommended point' reading came from the inverted-detuning chi

constraints.meaning: the achievable kappa window is bracketed from below by C2 and from above by C3 together with the two dispersivity caps. Above f01 the bracket is EMPTY (eta_max = 0). Inside the gap-protection window below f01 it reopens, and the efficiency ceiling there is 0.3115 at f_r = 37.489 GHz -- roughly three times the superseded 11.5 % corner, which was an artifact of the chi sign error rather than a physical squeeze. A genuine Purcell filter still relieves C3, and higher Q_i still relieves C2.

constraints.name: drive-tone pair-breaking window (P3)
constraints.meaning: with the drive plane pinned at 145 GHz the qubit may only be gated over a 0.29 GHz span of f01. Combined with C1-C4, the readout plane is the only tunable degree of freedom left; the 23.7-40.6 GHz tunability claim requires moving the drive plane, not the readout plane.

constraints.name: lattice mutual transparency (P5 geometry)
constraints.statement: f_r sits far below the drive lattice's TE gap and 145 GHz sits far above the readout lattice's fundamental gap
constraints.meaning: each cavity must carry its own complete mirror region; the only topology that keeps both field maxima on one island is the nested concept C, and that costs readout mirror rows.

constraints.name: 1-2-line dispersivity (P5, new; chi-convention ruling)
constraints.statement: (g12/Delta_12)^2 <= 0.01 with g12 = g n12/n01 and Delta_12 = f_r - f12
constraints.meaning: the corrected optimum sits between / near the two transmon lines, where the 0-1 dispersivity test is NOT the binding one: the exact 1-2 coupling is g12 = 1.38523 g and the 1-2 detuning is small. Imposing the same 0.01 the design already imposes on the 0-1 line makes the band f_r ~ 38.15-39.44 GHz INFEASIBLE (not merely marginal): at f_r = 39.2589 GHz -- the ruling's own candidate -- the largest admissible kappa falls to 1.881 MHz, below kappa_int = 2.687 MHz. The optimum therefore moves BELOW the 1-2 line.

constraints.name: two-pole robustness screen (P5, new; truth standard)
constraints.meaning: the corrected single formula is exact only in the harmonic limit (n12/n01)^2 -> 2; at E_J/E_C = 100 it overstates |chi| by about 8 % at the recommended detuning. The ruling designates the exact two-pole form the truth standard, so the recommended point is required to clear chi/kappa >= 1 under BOTH constructions. Dropping this screen (module flag TWO_POLE_SCREEN) moves the optimum to the koch_only_optimum block, which reaches eta = 0.3413 but has a two-pole chi/kappa of only 0.9315.

operating_envelope.envelope_statement: The two-cavity chip is feasible, but not where the superseded artifact put it. Once the P2 divider and the shared C_Sigma budget are enforced, the naive 22-point readout window collapses; once the measured internal-Q floor C2 is added, every kappa = 1 MHz point disappears. With the CORRECTED dispersive shift (Delta = f01 - f_r) the analytic ceiling C3 inverts its monotonicity and saturates at 2.9428 MHz above f01, below kappa_int everywhere in the mandated 4-16 GHz window: THE ENTIRE f_r > f01 READOUT WINDOW IS EMPTY, analytically, for any g and any d_eff. What survives is a corner BELOW the qubit, inside the gap-protection window [33.089, 42.811] GHz over which the Maxwell-scaled readout lattice's own TE gap covers f01: f_r ~ 37.439 GHz (Delta_r = -3.158 GHz, i.e. 1.525 GHz below the 1-2 line), d_eff_r ~ 60.0 um, kappa_r ~ 3.70 MHz, at a readout port efficiency of 30.7% -- about three times the 11.5% quoted before the correction, which was an artifact of the sign error, not a physical squeeze. That electrode still sits below the C_Sigma oversubscription knee at 86.9 um. Two new constraints bind here and did not before: C7, the 1-2-line dispersivity cap, which empties the band just below f01 that the ruling had flagged only as marginal; and C8, the requirement that the exact two-pole chi clears chi/kappa >= 1 too. The remaining hard external constraint is unchanged: C5, the 145 GHz drive plane pins the qubit to a 0.29 GHz window of f01, so gate-based frequency allocation and a fixed 145 GHz drive cavity are mutually exclusive regardless of anything the readout plane does.
escape_hatches: genuine Purcell filter at f_r: lifts C3, frees kappa_r and eta
higher Q_i (larger cell / better vertical confinement): lowers C2, optimistic ceiling Q_i = 18419 gives kappa_int = 2.033 MHz
drive plane moved below 147 GHz: lifts C5 entirely

relaxing C7 from 0.01 to the 0.0186 the ruling's candidate needs would reopen f_r ~ 39.26 GHz, but at a 1-2-line dispersivity 1.9x worse than the design allows on the 0-1 line -- an owner decision, not a default
